subject.title: Memory system: Cannot delete stale memories, conflicting entries persist

question: Should OpenClaw resolve this issue with a narrow model-visible recall UUID handoff, wait for the broader memory lifecycle contract, or deliberately split those two tracks?
rationale: Current source proves a narrow deletion-selector bug, while the issue also asks for conflict replacement/deprecation semantics that affect durable memory behavior and plugin API expectations.

options.title: Split narrow handoff from lifecycle design
options.body: Approve a focused memory-lancedb recall-to-forget selector fix and keep replacement/deprecation/conflict behavior in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/42650.

options.title: Design lifecycle first
options.body: Keep this issue blocked until the memory lifecycle contract defines forget, supersede, tombstone, and conflict behavior across memory plugins.

options.title: Defer the narrow fix
options.body: Accept the current extra `memory_forget(query=...)` round trip and leave this issue open only as evidence for the broader lifecycle work.

recommendation.title: Split narrow handoff from lifecycle design
recommendation.body: Approve a focused memory-lancedb recall-to-forget selector fix and keep replacement/deprecation/conflict behavior in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/42650.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent current-main ownership signal for the memory-lancedb implementation path where the narrow selector decision would land.
